title: Cost Disease
equation: Cost Growth = Economy Wage Growth - Sector Productivity Growth
hook: Nothing about your service changed, but it costs more to deliver every single year.
statement: Work that can't be sped up gets more expensive as the rest of the economy gets faster.
explainer: When other industries get more productive, wages rise everywhere. Hands-on work like coaching or care still takes the same hours, so it costs more for the same output. That quietly eats your margin.
sop: List the parts of your business where output per hour barely improves.
Estimate Economy Wage Growth for the people you hire.
Estimate Sector Productivity Growth for that work. Be honest, it's often near zero.
Subtract to find your yearly Cost Growth.
Raise prices on a schedule or redesign how you deliver.
equation_example: Wages across the economy rise 4% a year. Your service gets 1% more productive. 4% - 1% = 3%, so your costs creep up about 3% a year with zero change in quality. Bigger gap, faster creep. Smaller gap, flatter costs.
question: Pick one service you sell and write down when you last raised its price.
closing_statement: The work machines can't rush deserves to be priced right.
caption:
Principle Nº 336: Cost Disease

Nothing about your service changed, but it costs more to deliver every single year.

Work that can't be sped up gets more expensive as the rest of the economy gets faster.
